topic_title: Chapter 4 - Lesson 4-2 - Information Design and User Experience for Websites

questions.question: A persona is a typical user image set up as a concrete person.
A wireframe is the final decorated visual design of a website.
Proximity means placing related information close together so it is perceived as a group.
User-Centered Design prioritizes the creator's convenience over the user's needs.
What is the term for a typical user represented as a concrete person?
What is the term for a blueprint used to determine the placement and priority of information?
Match each description with the correct CRAP principle: A Contrast, B Repetition, C Alignment, D Proximity.

items.text: Highlight important information so it stands out.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the CRAP principles?
Which best describes User-Centered Design (UCD)?
options: Choose visual design before understanding users.
Begin from what the user needs and the situation in which the site will be used.
Always use the newest web technologies.

questions.question: Explain why a designer creates a persona and a wireframe before choosing colors and fonts.
questions.model_answer: A persona keeps the design focused on a concrete user's needs. A wireframe determines the placement and priority of information before visual preferences, making discussion and agreement with stakeholders easier.

questions.question: A school results page is cluttered and parents cannot quickly find grades. Suggest one persona, one wireframe decision, and one CRAP principle that could improve the page.
questions.model_answer: The persona could be a parent checking a child's grades. The wireframe could place grades in a high-priority block. Contrast could be used to make the grades stand out, or proximity could group related results.
